conviction_note: The findings net +0.8: the year-over-year brand-partner comparison eases from -31% in Q1 (5,300 vs 7,700) to about -10% in Q2 (about 5,200 maintained vs 5,800), and opex is down 28%. That argument rests on public numbers, with no consensus and a stock that has fallen after 6 of its last 7 prints, including Q1, when partners rose 20% sequentially and pre-tax loss was flat (-3.18%). So the scaled number is p_up 45 x abs 4.5 = -0.45. The sign disagrees with impact_sum because the reaction function (this name sells its prints) vetoes the mildly positive fundamental read.
bar: No consensus could be sourced; no analyst estimate was found and the company gives no numeric guidance (https://www.newsfilecorp.com/release/304633). The reference used is prior-year Q2 FY26 net revenue of $4,621,100 (https://www.newsfilecorp.com/release/269893). The estimate is about $4.3-4.5m. Because the bar is unsourced, every finding is capped small.
positioning_check: Short interest is about 11.9k shares at the 2026-06-30 settlement, days to cover about 1.0, borrow fee 5.9% (https://curvedtrading.com/stocks/educ/, updated 2026-07-14). Equibles shows 5,892 shares at 2026-03-13 (https://equibles.com/stocks/educ/shortinterest). That is under 0.2% of float, so not crowded. There is no options market, so no skew (baseline options.status no_options_market). Run-up is +1.15% over 20 days and the stock is 6% off its 52-week low. Turnover is about $26k a day.

findings.finding: The brand-partner comparison eases sharply. Q2 FY26 averaged 5,800 active PaperPie brand partners. Partners were 5,200 at end-May 2026, and the CEO said on July 9 that 'we have maintained this level of brand partners to this day'. Q2 partners are therefore down about 10% YoY, against -31% in Q1, when revenue fell 33%. The prior-year Q2 was also hit by lender-imposed purchasing restrictions that caused out-of-stocks, now lifted. Revenue decline should narrow to roughly -3% to -10% against $4.62m.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: In Q1 FY27 (2026-07-09) revenue fell 33% YoY but partners rose 20% sequentially; the stock fell 3.18%. In Q2 FY26 (2025-10-09) revenue fell 29% while the loss narrowed; the stock fell 9.94%. Six of the last 7 prints were down (baseline).
findings.why_not_priced: No analyst publishes an estimate and the stock trades about $26k a day. If the market had priced a sharply narrower revenue decline, the name would not sit 6% off its 52-week low with a flat 20-day tape into a print it has sold 6 of 7 times. Still, the arithmetic is public, so this is inference, not a hidden number.
findings.independence: Q1 call transcript, CEO on partners maintained (https://www.webull.com/news/15219109458093056, 2026-07-09). Q1 FY27 10-Q MD&A on lender purchasing restrictions in the first three quarters of FY26 causing out-of-stocks (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/31667/000118518526002870/educ10q053126.htm, 2026-07-09). Same company, different documents.

findings.finding: The cost base is structurally lower. Q1 FY27 total operating expenses were $4.10m vs $5.70m (-28%), G&A $2.07m vs $2.69m, and gross margin 59.3% vs 58.2%. A G&A cut of more than $1.2m for FY27 is planned. Applied to a Q2 revenue decline of about 5%, the Q2 pre-tax loss should narrow from $(1.75)m in Q2 FY26 toward roughly $(1.0)-(1.3)m.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q1 FY27 opex fell 28% and the stock still fell 3.18%. Q2 FY26 pre-tax loss narrowed from $(2.47)m to $(1.75)m and the stock fell 9.94%. This name has not paid for cost cuts.
findings.why_not_priced: Nobody models the quarter. A priced narrowing would show as a recovery off the 52-week low into the print, which has not happened (-20% from high, +6% from low). The same document already showed it once, though, and the market did not reward it.
findings.independence: Q1 release, cost reduction plan above $1.2m (https://www.newsfilecorp.com/release/304633/Educational-Development-Corporation-Announces-Fiscal-2027-First-Quarter-Results, 2026-07-09). Same company, overlapping source with the 10-Q.

findings.finding: A full valuation allowance removes the tax benefit. Q1 FY27 tax expense was $16,500 against a $374,100 benefit a year earlier, so pre-tax loss was flat but net loss widened to $(0.16) from $(0.13) per share. Q2 FY26 carried about $0.46m of benefit (pre-tax $(1.75)m, net $(1.29)m), so headline net loss per share will compare worse than pre-tax by about $0.05.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: In Q1 FY27, the first print with the allowance, a widening headline net loss on flat pre-tax coincided with -3.18%.
findings.why_not_priced: This is below-the-line optics on a name with no estimate. It is sized as a fraction because it has no path to cash or guidance; the CFO said the allowance reverses on a return to profit.
findings.independence: 10-Q income tax note (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/31667/000118518526002870/educ10q053126.htm). Same company, two documents.

findings.finding: The Q1 10-Q discloses that EDC did not meet Usborne's minimum purchase requirements and did not supply the letter of credit, so Usborne may terminate on less than 30 days' notice. Usborne also refuses to pay a $1.0m FY22 rebate. Usborne was 33.1% of PaperPie product revenue and $19.6m of inventory. The Q2 10-Q will restate this status.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No prior print turned visibly on this disclosure; it has sat in filings through several -3% reactions.
findings.why_not_priced: It is largely priced: the risk is in prior filings and Usborne has given no notice. The residual is the chance that the Q2 10-Q reports a change. There is no sign of one, so it is sized near zero.

findings.finding: Liquidity is not under pressure. Q1 operating cash flow was +$0.56m from inventory liquidation, cash $1.66m plus $0.15m restricted, and the $2.0m Regent Bank revolver is undrawn, maturing 2027-03-06, with no going-concern language. The bank debt was cleared by the Hilti sale-leaseback.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The Q2 FY26 print (2025-10-09) announced the building sale to clear bank debt and still fell 9.94%.
findings.why_not_priced: It mostly is. The only new element in the window is whether the 10-Q adds a going-concern flag within 12 months of the revolver's maturity. None is expected, given the inventory-to-cash conversion.
findings.independence: Q1 call, CFO: 'the plan is to be cash flow positive' (https://www.webull.com/news/15219109458093056).

findings.finding: Publishers Weekly reports that children's books were the only category whose print sales grew YoY in Q1 2026 (Circana BookScan). This is a weak end-market proxy for an MLM channel whose decline is driven by partner count.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Unavailable; no prior print turned on industry data.
findings.why_not_priced: It is a proxy with no company or counterparty confirmation, and it covers Jan-Mar, not EDUC's Jun-Aug quarter. It is sized at almost nothing.

searched_and_found_nothing: The Q2 FY27 release is not out at search time (~17:30 UTC). Only the call notice exists (https://www.newsfilecorp.com/release/313730, 2026-09-09).
EDGAR 8-Ks since 2026-06: only call notices (06-16, 09-09), Q1 2.02 (07-09) and annual meeting 5.07 (07-14). No reverse split, no Nasdaq notice, no material agreement.
No dated PaperPie fall 2026 recruiting promotions or brand-partner counts after July 2026.
No 2026 Usborne agreement change or termination notice.
Nasdaq short-interest API returned 503; aggregators were used instead.
baseline_tension: There is no skew and the run-up is flat. The mildly positive comparison and cost evidence cut against the name's own reaction history (6 of 7 prints down, median |3.18%|), so p_up sits at 45 rather than above 50.
lessons_applied: Lesson 1 (verified fact is not a reaction; this name sells prints, Q1 fell 3.18% on improving partners and flat pre-tax): brand-partner comparison finding cut +1.0 to +0.6, opex finding +0.5 to +0.4.
Lesson 2 (one-off below operating income): valuation-allowance tax optics cut -0.3 to -0.2.
Lesson 4 (financing is a question): the answer is the cash comes from inventory liquidation and the revolver is undrawn, so the finding is cut +0.2 to +0.1 and the sign is kept non-negative.
Lesson 6 (unsourced bar): every finding is held within +/-0.6; the bar is stated as unsourced, with prior-year revenue as reference.
Lesson 8 (understatement): abs_move_pct raised from 4.0 to 4.5, since the last Q2 print moved 9.94%. expected_move -0.4 becomes -0.45.
Lesson 7: short interest checked, not crowded; there are no negative findings large enough for it to matter.
